claim: Expected free energy is defined as extrinsic value plus epistemic value (expected information gain), and epistemic value is the theory's definition of curiosity.
agent_test: Compute expected information gain over a hypothesis set for each candidate probe; compare to unscored probe choice at equal tokens.

claim: In active inference the explore-to-exploit switch is built into the maths: the epistemic term is expected information gain, it shrinks as uncertainty is resolved, and preferences then decide (Friston 2015 abstract, opened). Shown only in simulation (T-maze, rule learning); it holds only if the model is right. No human or LLM test by these papers.
agent_test: Stop open mode when the estimated information gain of the best probe falls under a threshold; compare to fixed-budget exploration.

claim: The epistemic term is a design choice, not a theorem: the natural future free energy penalises information seeking, and EFE adds the bonus. Active inference authors keep ambiguity in G; others offer variants.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; use as warning that no single curiosity formula exists.

claim: Active inference with an epistemic term explores without a hand-tuned bonus in small grid and control tasks; with no reward, belief-based agents keep exploring while Q-learning stalls.
agent_test: Compare an information-gain probe score with a plain novelty or random probe score on a small search task.

claim: Epistemic bonuses do not always help: no benefit on tasks where random actions find reward, and a deep active-inference agent with the epistemic term failed dSprites while reward-only variants solved it.
agent_test: Include a no-bonus arm; use exploration only when a quick greedy attempt has failed.

claim: Humans use two exploration mechanisms: an information bonus (directed) and decision noise (random), both rising with the number of remaining choices. Brain-stimulation and development studies dissociate them, and a hybrid model competes.
agent_test: Vary the stated remaining budget in the prompt and check whether the agent shifts probe choice toward uncertain options.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Off-the-shelf LLMs explore poorly in bandits: in Krishnamurthy 2024 the >60% suffix-failure rate for GPT-4 with a basic prompt is from the T=500 figure; the main experiments use T=100, K=5, gap 0.2, where only 3 GPT-4 configurations avoid suffix failure, 2 of those fail the other way (uniform-like) and 1 succeeds. Newer models (2025-26) explore more with thinking on but still fail directed exploration in non-stationary tasks (d02, d03, d14).
agent_test: Run a bandit-style probe task with the plain prompt and measure suffix failure rate.

claim: Prompt-only repairs help but stay below classical algorithms: externally computed per-arm summaries, algorithm-guided hints and few-shot demonstrations raise win-rate (Gemini Pro raw 45.5, summarised 60.0, guided 59.6, UCB 90.6). Note: the EVOLvE few-shot Flash win-rate 50.2 uses summarised-history demonstrations, not algorithm-guided ones; an extra try-all sweep was the biggest single gain in Schmied 2025 (Gemma2 27B near UCB).
agent_test: Give the agent a coded tally of probes and outcomes versus raw transcript; measure share of best-option pulls at equal tokens.

claim: Small models (Gemma 2B/9B) gain nothing from guidance, and guidance can hurt (few-shot Pro contextual bandit guided 25.0 vs flash 60.7), so the benefit depends on model size. New: a forced try-all sweep helped across Gemma2 sizes (d01), Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B showed too little exploration in a pilot while Qwen3-14B matched 32B (d14), so guidance not helping small models is not the whole story.
agent_test: Test the scaffold at two model sizes.

claim: GPT-3 on the horizon task showed no directed exploration (horizon effect beta=-0.15, p=.58) and no noise scaling with horizon, though regret was lower than humans on average (2.72 vs 3.24).
agent_test: Not repeated on current models in opened sources; replicate with a current model and chain of thought.

claim: In-context exploration by LLMs improves with meta-learning across tasks but through prior calibration and greed, not more curiosity.
agent_test: Check whether showing earlier solved tasks changes probe diversity or just exploitation speed.

claim: Scoring candidate questions by expected information gain computed outside the LLM raises success in closed-set question games: UoT +38.1% average over direct prompting (the paper does not say whether this is relative or percentage points; table cells suggest relative) (GPT-4 troubleshooting 43.7 to 67.3), DPO on EIG pairs +10 to +12 points, LIPS EIG from 0.65 at k=1 to above human mean 1.27 by k=10.
agent_test: Sample k candidate probes, estimate answer partition over hypotheses, pick max entropy reduction; compare with first-sample probe at equal tokens.

claim: Information-gain selection works best with a closed hypothesis set; in open sets gains are smaller and the answer model assumes clean elimination.
agent_test: Test the probe selector on open versus closed problems.

claim: Curiosity needs a filter: novelty-only or learning-progress-only drives chase trivia or noise; LLM-judged interestingness or sensible goals fix this (ELLM <3 vs 6 achievements; OMNI beats learning progress; Voyager random curriculum cut items 93%).
agent_test: Add a relevance check to probe choice (does the answer bear on the goal) and compare with raw novelty.

claim: An LLM-written curriculum of novel-but-achievable tasks drives sustained exploration: Voyager 63 items, 3.3x more than baselines, only agent reaching diamond (1 of 3 runs).
agent_test: Three runs per method only; replicate with more seeds.

claim: Pure input-entropy curiosity rewards unlearnable noise; information gain about a latent falls to zero when nothing can be learned, which guards against the noisy-TV trap.
agent_test: Insert an unlearnable distractor in a task and check whether the agent keeps probing it.

claim: Active-inference controllers wrapped around LLMs (Prakki 2024, PUMA 2026, F-Explorer) exist, but none isolates the epistemic term's effect on accuracy at equal compute.
agent_test: Ablate the epistemic weight (lambda_e 0 vs 0.4) in an LLM loop at equal tokens.

claim: Standard active inference is reward-optimal only for planning horizon 1; deeper horizons need recursive (sophisticated) inference, which makes epistemic choice more confident in the T-maze.
agent_test: Compare one-step against lookahead probe scoring.

claim: Directed information-seeking by humans on the horizon task was supported by a small student sample (N=30): the measured information bonus was larger than an optimal model would use, and the noise was not optimal. A second sample (Zajkowski 2017, N=31, same lab, TMS) also showed a horizon-driven information bonus that was cut by right frontopolar inhibition while decision noise stayed unchanged. No failed replication of the Horizon task was found; a 2025 tDCS null (N=43) used a different task.
agent_test: Treat as weak; see Gershman 2018 hybrid account.

claim: Human eye-movement data favour models with the epistemic term over preference-only models (pooled log evidence ~888), but heuristics were added by hand and the sample size is not recorded.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent.

claim: An explicit stop rule beats a fixed budget at equal average cost when sampling answers: Adaptive-Consistency (threshold 0.95) cut samples up to 7.9x with <0.1% average accuracy drop on 17 datasets and beat uniform self-consistency at equal average samples; answer-convergence stopping cut tokens >40% on NaturalQuestions but was unstable on MATH-500 and GPQA. Not yet tested on open-ended probes.
agent_test: Stop S3 when the leading hypothesis passes a coded confidence test or the best probe's estimated gain is under a threshold, with a minimum probe count; compare to a fixed probe budget at equal tokens on a task with an open hypothesis space.

claim: For open hypothesis spaces, the workable estimate of expected information gain is: let the LLM sample N (about 20) candidate hypotheses, filter them against the evidence so far, weight them equally, and compute the gain in code. Weighting by the LLM's own sample log-probabilities was clearly worse (Kobalczyk 2025). LLM-implemented posterior sampling and one-step information-directed probes also work in small spaces (Arumugam 2026).
agent_test: Compare uniform-weighted sampled hypotheses with LLM-estimated partitions for probe choice on an open task, at equal tokens.

claim: Coded coverage helps more than prompt advice: a forced try-every-option sweep gave the largest gain in Schmied 2025 (Gemma2 27B nearly closed the gap to UCB; 10-arm coverage only 40-65% without it), and the LLM is better used as a proposer of candidate probes than as the tracker or scorer (Harris & Slivkins 2026; Berdica 2026).
agent_test: Force a first sweep of all candidate probes, keep a coded tally, and compare with a raw-transcript baseline at equal tokens.

claim: An LLM-judged interest filter on top of a learnability signal beat learnability alone and uniform sampling on Crafter (OMNI). It has not been shown to beat raw novelty at equal tokens on unlearnable distractors, and the judge carries human taste. A prediction-error curiosity bonus (the noisy-TV-prone signal) helped only with narrow training data (In-Context Curiosity).
agent_test: Add an unlearnable distractor probe class; compare novelty-only, gain-falling-to-zero, and LLM-relevance filter at equal tokens.

claim: Thinking raises directed exploration in 2025-26 models but the picture is mixed: o3-mini at high thinking exceeded the human level of directed exploration in a stationary 2-armed task, yet no thinking model reached effective directed exploration in a non-stationary 4-armed task; labels and reward sign still bias exploration even in a frontier thinking model.
agent_test: Give the remaining budget as a number and the tally as code; measure whether probe count rises with the budget.

claim: Friston 2015 and Friston 2017 are simulation-only: a T-maze (128 trials per setting, four schemes) and an abstract rule-learning task (32 trials, 64 artificial agents). Neither ran a human experiment nor an LLM test; both state curiosity as the decay of expected information gain.
agent_test: Treat as theory support only; justify the S3 stop rule with d09, d10 and d11 instead.

claim: Beyond Wilson 2014 (N=30), the horizon-driven information bonus appears in Zajkowski 2017 (N=31, same lab), and Gershman 2018 (N=45) and Chakroun 2020 (N=31) data were re-fitted in Zhang 2025. No failed replication of the Horizon task was found, but no independent-lab effect sizes were read, so the claim stays weak.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; use as background only.
